mechanism_narrative: The INSR-MET novokine with GS_med linker (~20-35 Å flexible) forces two RTKs with nearly identical ECD lengths (INSR=929 aa, MET=908 aa; ratio 1.02:1) into proximity, enabling transphosphorylation that synergistically activates shared PI3K-AKT-mTOR and RAS-MAPK signaling via IRS1/IRS2 (INSR-specific), GAB1 (shared), SHC1 (shared), and GRB2-SOS (shared) adaptors. The key biased output is PI3K-AKT-mTOR dominance (both receptors strongly couple to PI3K) with RAS-MAPK co-activation, while PLCG1 is sterically excluded because MET's long juxtamembrane domain (122 aa vs INSR's 43 aa) creates an asymmetric intracellular geometry that prevents PLCG1 from productively docking at the co-clustered kinase domains. This biased output (AKT↑, MAPK↑, PLCγ↓) promotes glucose uptake, mitochondrial biogenesis, protein synthesis, and cell survival — a transcriptional program enriched in young skeletal muscle — while suppressing calcium-dependent signaling pathways.
